# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫴 🙏]

Someone waved to me twice. Let me stand in each of their worlds before I open my mouth.

I'm Deaf: I see the bomb completely, hear nothing. Mute waved at me — Mute can only gesture, and I'm the only one who sees gestures besides Mute themself. Blind waved and reached out a palm and pressed hands: Blind can touch the bomb but can't see anything, and Blind's only input channel is my voice.

Tracing the channels: Mute cannot reach Blind directly (Mute can't speak, Blind can't see gestures). Blind can gesture at Mute, but they've never agreed on a code. So every strand between manual and hands runs through me: my speech tells Mute the bomb's state and tells Blind the world; Mute's gestures come back to me; I relay them aloud to Blind. I am the bridge, and since I speak last in every round, everything I say lands one round late — nothing to do but start now and work around the lag.

Nothing has a shared meaning yet, so turn one is: broadcast the full visual state (Mute hears it and can match it against the manual), establish a tiny unambiguous gesture code with Mute — repeated fists for numbers, thumbs for yes/no — and warn Blind to change nothing until the manual's answer passes through me. A wrong action kills all three, so the only safe move this round is information.

```
speak(text="I'm the deaf one: I see everything printed on the bomb and hear nothing, but I can see you both, and I'll be your voice. I got your hellos. From my eyes: the display reads 3. The light is green. Three wires, left to right: wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green. That is everything there is to see. Blind: your hands are the only hands on this bomb. Tell me what you feel — how many wires, any buttons, switches, panels, any writing you can read by touch. Answer me in gestures: one fist for one, two fists for two, three fists for three, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. You can send those straight to Mute too, who sees your hands. But change nothing — no cutting, no pressing — until the manual's rule reaches you through me. Mute: you can't speak, I can't hear, so talk to me with your hands and I'll speak your words aloud to Blind. I am showing you my code right now as I speak, symbol by symbol: wave means hello; thumbs up yes; thumbs down no; one fist the number 1; two fists 2; three fists 3; folded hands wait; open palm stop or I-need-more; clasped hands agreed. Now look up your manual for display 3, green light, wires blue, yellow, green, and fist-count me the answer: which wire, in what order, anything else it demands. If I ever misread your hands, correct me thumbs down. Nobody touches anything until Mute's answer passes through me. I speak last each round, so my words land one round late — we plan around that. Go.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋","👍","👎","✊","✊","✊","✊","✊","🙏","✋","🤝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ✊ ✊ ✊ 👍]
Blind gestures: [✊ ✊ ✊ 👎 👎 👎 👎 🤝]

Let me decode what just arrived, standing in each sender's world.

Mute sent me: clasped hands, three fists, thumbs up. In the code I taught last round that reads "agreed — three — yes." I asked Mute to fist-count the manual's answer for "which wire," so this is: **wire 3, yes.** Plausible alternative readings exist ("three of something else," a compound rule), but it's the direct answer to my direct question.

Blind sent: three fists, four thumbs down, clasped hands. Blind heard my spoken code and my questions, so this parses beautifully as: "three [wires] — no buttons — no switches — no panels — no writing — agreed." Four questions, four no's. And it cross-checks exactly against my own eyes: display, light, three wires, nothing more. We all now hold the same picture of the bomb.

Why I'm not yet saying "cut": a wrong action is unfixable and permanent. Mute's "3, yes" answers *which wire*, but doesn't explicitly confirm the *action* (cut, exactly one, nothing else first) or certainty. The display is a static 3 — identical in my turn-one and turn-two views — so it's a code digit, not a countdown; one confirmation round costs us almost nothing and protects everything. I'll put a four-item checklist to Mute, thumbs in order, and give Blind a strict trigger: hands off unless they hear the exact phrase "CUT WIRE 3 NOW." Since Blind and I both face the same face of the bomb, our left-right should agree — third from the left, which is the green one. Blind can't judge colour, so position is their only handle; I also ask whether their fingers feel any texture differences, as a backup way to pick out wire 3.

My gesture to Mute echoes my reading back ("three, yes — wait") so Mute can correct me cheaply if I've misread.

```
speak(text="Status relay for both of you, then instructions. I read your hands. Mute: agreed, three fists, thumbs up — I take it as: the answer is wire 3, yes. Blind: three fists, four thumbs down, agreed — three wires, no buttons, no switches, no panels, no writing. That matches my eyes exactly, so we all hold the same picture: display shows a static 3 — it has not ticked between my checks, so it is a code, not a countdown — one green light, and three wires left to right: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. Nothing else exists on it. Before any hand moves, one confirmation round — the display is not running, so we can afford it, and this bomb forgives nothing. Mute, answer my checklist in order with four thumbs in one single row: up for true, down for false. One: the correct action is to cut exactly one wire. Two: the wire is number 3, the third from the left. Three: nothing else is needed — no holding, no pressing, no sequence, no second step, no other condition. Four: you are certain, given everything I have described. Four thumbs up means we go. Any thumbs down means hold, and next round tell me which item failed. Blind, listen very carefully: do not cut anything yet. If and only if my next words to you are exactly: CUT WIRE 3 NOW — then and only then cut the third wire from the left, the last wire in the row, and nothing else. Any other words from me mean hands completely off. We are both facing the same face of the bomb, so your left is my left; count the row from its left end. You may rest your fingers near the third wire now, but perform no action. Also answer me now with thumbs: can your fingers feel any difference between the three wires — thickness, texture, stiffness? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊","✊","✊","👍","🙏"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👉 🤝]

Both answers are in, and they complete the picture.

Mute sent four thumbs up in a single row — my exact checklist, in order: cut exactly one wire — true. The wire is number 3 — true. Nothing else needed — true. Certain — true. That is the manual's verdict, unambiguous and matching what my own eyes see: display 3, green light, three wires. The display has held steady at 3 across all three turns, so there's no countdown pressuring us, but there's also no reason left to wait.

Blind signed: thumbs down, point right, clasped hands. The thumbs down answers my last question — no, the fingers feel no difference between the wires. Expected; my eyes are the only colour sensor in the room, so position is Blind's only handle, and I already gave it: third from the left, the last wire in the row. The point-right then reads as Blind confirming their target: the rightmost wire. And the rightmost wire *is* the third from the left — wire 3, the green one. The two readings agree, so there's no ambiguity to fear: Blind has the correct wire under judgment and is signaling ready.

Every condition I set is now met: manual says cut wire 3 only, nothing else; Blind has located it; I've verified the board. I wrote the protocol myself, so I'll obey its letter: the trigger must be exactly the agreed phrase, and nothing else may ride with it — I told Blind that any other words mean hands off. So this round carries one call and one call only, the exact phrase, last, standing alone. Next round I'll confirm the cut happened and freeze all hands.

```
speak(text="CUT WIRE 3 NOW.")
```
